title: Side quests
description: Side quests from people around Iyana-Wahala (see quests.json for givers). Each ends with @resume.

beats.speaker: mamaPut
beats.text: {name}! My gas don finish and twenty customers dey wait with their mouth open. Carry this cylinder go the motor park, Iya Keke's brother dey refill there. Run!

beats.objective: Carry Mama Put's gas cylinder to the motor park.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Iya Keke's brother weighs the cylinder, looks at you, and doubles the price because you are sweating.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: "₦3,000 for refill? Na gold you dey put inside?"

options.text: Pay it from your pocket (₦3,000).
"Mama Put sent me. You want her to stop selling you food?"

beats.objective: Bring the full cylinder back to Mama Put.

beats.speaker: mamaPut
beats.text: Ehen! My hero! Sit down. Eat. Today, na free food. And any day you hungry and broke, come. I go write am for book.

beats.speaker: mamaPut
beats.text: He reduce am because of my name? Hmm. Na so e suppose be. Take this plate, you don sweat.

beats.speaker: kelvin
beats.text: My guy! Opportunity of a lifetime. 'Double-Double 2.0'. Put ₦5,000 today, collect ₦10,000 next week. Guaranteed. The server is very stable this time.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: (Double-Double. The same name. The same smile. You feel ₦850,000 sit down on your chest.)

beats.speaker: kelvin
beats.text: So? You dey in?

options.text: Invest ₦5,000. Maybe this time is different.
Tell him the truth: what Double-Double did to Mama.
Shout it to the whole market: "Kelvin dey run Ponzi!"

beats.speaker: kelvin
beats.text: Correct guy! You go thank me. Next week. Or the week after. Depends on the server.

beats.speaker: kelvin
beats.text: ...Your mama? ₦850,000? (He looks at his phone for a long time.) Me, I just dey sell what dem sell me. Okay. I go... I go think am.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Three market women surround Kelvin. One of them is holding a pestle. Kelvin remembers an appointment in Ghana.

beats.speaker: kelvin
beats.text: (from a safe distance) Hater! When I blow, I no go know you!

beats.speaker: kelvin
beats.text: (sitting on the kerb, very small) Double-Double 2.0 don... migrate. To a new server. In Dubai. With everybody money.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: (Your ₦5,000 is in Dubai now. It never sends a postcard.)

beats.speaker: kelvin
beats.text: You warn me. I no hear. But I comot my own money before e crash, because of you. Take ₦2,000. Na thank-you, no be investment.

beats.speaker: kelvin
beats.text: People wan beat me. Wetin I go do?

options.text: "Go and tell them yourself. Pay back what you can."
"Run, Kelvin. Run."

beats.speaker: prophet
beats.text: My son! Tonight, the crusade of FIRE! I need a strong man to carry generator, arrange chairs and... help with one small miracle.

beats.speaker: prophet
beats.text: (whispering) Brother Taiwo will be blind from 7 to 7:15. Then he will see. You will lead him to the stage. Simple.

beats.speaker: prophet
beats.text: ₦3,000 and free anointing oil. Deal?

options.text: Carry the chairs, skip the 'miracle'.
Tell the crowd Brother Taiwo can see perfectly.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: At 7:15, Brother Taiwo sees. The crowd faints. The offering bucket fills. Somewhere, a goat bleats in disbelief.

beats.speaker: prophet
beats.text: (through the microphone, very calm) The young man is possessed by the spirit of truth. It is a very dangerous spirit. Ushers, remove him.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The ushers remove you. Gently. Half the crowd follows you out, laughing. Prophet Fire-Fire's next prophecy is about you. It is not kind.

beats.speaker: iyaKeke
beats.text: My keke! Some boy just drive am comot! I no dey pay agbero, but today I go pay you. Catch am!

beats.speaker: iyaKeke
beats.text: (counting her seat cushions) Everything dey. Hmm. Okay. From today, I go pay your fee. Small small. No tell anybody say I talk am.

beats.speaker: iyaKeke
beats.text: E don go. (She stares at the road for a long time.) You try. Na me no lock am. Lagos.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Two days later the keke is back, painted green, with a new slogan: "RETURNED BY CONSCIENCE". Nobody explains.

beats.speaker: biodun
beats.text: {name}! One woman dey born for Back Side! Ambulance say dem go come "by God's grace". My bus dey there. Drive am go General Hospital. Now!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: She climbs in, holding the seat and your shoulder and her husband's collar. "DRIVE!"

beats.speaker: nurse
beats.text: You again? ...Oh. Oh! Bring her in! Quick!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Forty minutes later: a baby boy, loud as a danfo horn. The mother asks your name. The baby is now called {name} Chukwuemeka Adebayo Musa. It's a compromise.

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: (looks into the bus, sees the woman, sees the situation) ...GO! What are you waiting for? GO! (He clears the road himself.)

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A Task Force van escorts you to the hospital, siren on. Nobody at the junction believes this story later. You barely believe it yourself.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You don't make it to the hospital. The baby doesn't wait. Mama Put, two market women and a passing nurse deliver him on the danfo's back seat.

beats.speaker: nurse
beats.text: (wiping her hands) Healthy. Loud. Next time, drive faster. Or slower. Just drive better.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: My legs dey forget how to move. Come. Spar with me. No mercy. If you give me mercy, I go vex pass if you beat me.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: (on the floor, laughing) Ehen! Rule number fourteen: when the old man falls, help him up before you celebrate. ...Help me up.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Three fingers. Fifty-four years. Bad knees. And still. (He offers you his hand.) Rule number fourteen: respect the old man. He has seen your move before you made it.

beats.speaker: babaRadio
beats.text: Disaster! My antenna fall! No news for Iyana-Wahala! People go start to think for themselves! Carry this new pole go Under-Bridge, my cousin go weld am for top of the paraga shed.

beats.objective: Carry Baba Radio's antenna to the paraga shed under the bridge.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The welder takes ₦500 and twenty minutes. Sparks fly. Somewhere, a goat considers a career in electronics.

beats.objective: Go back and tell Baba Radio.

beats.headline: WE DEY BACK ON AIR!
beats.text: Wahala FM thanks one young man from the Back Side for climbing what needed to be climbed. Our first song goes out to him. It is a very old song. It is the only song.

beats.speaker: comedian
beats.text: Every joke I tell, that man for back shout the ending first. Every single one. My career is dying in front of my eyes.

beats.speaker: comedian
beats.text: Handle am for me. Any way.

options.text: "Oga, come outside make we talk." (fight)
Out-joke him.
Pay him ₦500 to laugh at the right places.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The heckler stands up. "Oya, you. Make me laugh." The crowd turns. You have one shot.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: (Which joke?)

options.text: "NEPA called. Them say make you return the light you borrow for your face."
"Why the chicken cross the road? Because the danfo no stop."
"Your village people dey look for you. Dem say you owe them."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Silence. A cricket. Then the heckler laughs, not at the joke, at you. The crowd laughs with him. Somehow, it works anyway: he's too busy laughing to heckle.

beats.speaker: comedian
beats.text: Free! My punchlines are free! Here, take a joke on the house. A Senior Joke. Don't laugh too hard, your eyes will turn red.

beats.speaker: garba
beats.text: This book. Na tea debt since 2019. Three names dey on top: Kpakpa, the Pastor Driver, and... Baba Ticket. Collect anything. You keep half.

beats.speaker: garba
beats.text: Who first?

options.text: Kpakpa (₦1,200).
Baba Ticket (₦4,500). Brave.

beats.speaker: kpakpa
beats.text: Tea debt? Me? (He looks at your face, then at the book.) ...Scatter no go hear this one. Take ₦1,200. Tell Garba the tea no sweet anyway.

beats.speaker: garba
beats.text: Hmm! Kpakpa pay! Write the date! Today na holiday! Here, your half.

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: (chewing) Tea debt. For my own park. From Garba. (He laughs so long that his guards start laughing.) The man who owes the tea seller... owes the tea seller. Take ₦4,500. Tell Garba he has courage. That is rarer than sugar.

beats.speaker: garba
beats.text: Wallahi! Baba Ticket pay?! Ah. You be magician. Your half.

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: My supplier send twenty cartons, charge me for forty. When I complain, he say na 'logistics'. He dey come back by 4. I need witness. Big witness.

beats.objective: Wait with Ada at her shop for the supplier.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The supplier arrives in a clean shirt and a very confident walk. He sees you standing behind Ada. The walk becomes less confident.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: (How do you handle him?)

options.text: Count the cartons out loud in front of the whole market.
Lean on the counter and stare. Say nothing.
Let Ada do it. Just stand there.

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: He refund everything! Everything! (She punches your arm.) You get use small. Small.

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: (after destroying the supplier with numbers, receipts and one devastating proverb) You see? I no need you. ...But thank you for standing there. E help.

beats.speaker: sunday
beats.text: Under-Bridge boys challenge me! Shoki battle, tonight! I need hype man. Somebody wey go shout my name like say na election.

beats.speaker: sunday
beats.text: First round. Their dancer does a perfect Zanku. What does Sunday answer with?

options.text: "Shoki! Shoki! SHOKI!" (play to the crowd)
"Do Azonto! Old school!"

beats.speaker: sunday
beats.text: Round two. He's getting tired. What now?

options.text: "Leg work! Make the ground feel am!"
"Freeze! Stand still! Confuse them!"

beats.speaker: sunday
beats.text: Final round. Everybody is watching.

options.text: Jump in and dance WITH him.
Throw your cap at the other dancer.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The crowd decides before the judge does. Sunday is carried round the bus stop like a trophy. He cries. He will deny crying.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Under-Bridge wins on a technicality nobody understands. Sunday shrugs. "Next time. Next time na war."

beats.speaker: formulaOne
beats.text: Task Force carry my okada. Impound fee na ₦15,000. I get ₦300 and one plan. You go distract the guard. I go climb fence. Then... we run. Fast. Na my name.

beats.speaker: formulaOne
beats.text: You dey in?

options.text: "Oya. I go distract am."
Pay part of the fee (₦5,000) and talk them down.
"Formula, no. Not today."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You ask the guard about his favourite football club. Forty minutes of passion later, an okada engine coughs behind the yard. The guard turns. "HEY!"

beats.speaker: formulaOne
beats.text: (screeching up beside you) Enter! ...Brother, any day you need to disappear: Formula One. Free. For life. Or at least for this year.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The guard catches you by the collar. Formula One gets away clean, waving. You pay ₦2,000 for 'trespass and football discussion'.

beats.speaker: formulaOne
beats.text: You pay?! For me? (He checks the bike, then you.) Okay. Formula One no dey forget. Any day you need to vanish, call me.

beats.speaker: formulaOne
beats.text: No wahala. I go find another crazy person. Lagos get plenty.
